Northside CNRA:
The Medium Density Residential classification predominates the Northside Area. A small area of Light Industrial is shown for the triangle easterly of Bayshore Freeway, with additional Light Industrial uses shown for the area between Taylor and Empire Streets at the westerly edge of the project area. High Density Residential and Public Park & Open Space are indicated in the area betweem Taylor Street, Bayshore Freeway, and the existing Fred Watson Park
Olinder CNRA:
The frontage along Santa Clara Street has the Neighborhood/Commercial designation, as does a small triangular area between 24th Street, William Street and the Western Pacific railroad tracks. The remainder of Olinder is Medium High Density (8-12 d.u./acre) and High Density Residential (12-25 d.u./acre) in the area bounded by San Fernando and 23rd Streets, and backing up to the Santa Clara Street commercial zone.
B. GEOLOGY AND SOILS
Introduction
The Community Development Block Grant program will be implemented in only four of San Jose's fifteen planning areas; Alum Rock, Alviso, Central, and the northern part of Willow Glen. The following description of geologic and soil characteristics will therefore be limited to these four areas. For greater detail and scope, the reader is directed to the <u>Technical Reports of the Geotechnical Investigation</u>, City of San Jose's Sphere of Influence (Cooper-Clark and Associates, 1974).
Topography
The site (Alum Rock, Alviso, Central, and Willow Glen Planning Areas) occupies the central portion of the northern Santa Clara Valley. This valley is a structural trough between the Mount Hamilton Range to the east and the Santa Cruz Mountains to the west. Relief throughout the area is very low, with a gentle northerly slope of less than 5%. Elevations range from 2 feet below sea level in Alviso to 140 ft. above sea level in the eastern portion of Alum Rock.
Subsurface
The valley floor is composed of alluvium deposited in past ages by the streams flowing from the surrounding mountains into San Francisco Bay. Interfluvial basin deposits occur in the low areas of the valley and have relatively poor bearing strength and are subject to settlement. Fluvial deposits are extensive in the San Jose area and can be subject to liquefaction of the sand lenses contained therein. Bay muds are located in Alviso adjacent to San Francisco Bay and have poor bearing strength and are subject to settlement.
